Rotations in two and three dimensions

Source: R/transformations.R
robot_rotation.Rd

Creates a validated rotation, an element of SO(2) or SO(3). Exactly one representation must be supplied:

robot_rotation(
  x = NULL,
  axis = NULL,
  angle = NULL,
  euler = NULL,
  sequence = "ZYX",
  rotvec = NULL,
  quaternion = NULL,
  tol = 1e-06
)

Arguments

x

Optional matrix, robot_rotation, or robot_quaternion.

axis

Rotation axis (length 3).

angle

Rotation angle in radians.

euler

Three Euler angles in radians.

sequence

Intrinsic axis sequence, one of the 12 valid sequences such as "ZYX", "XYZ" or "ZYZ".

rotvec

Rotation vector (length 3).

quaternion

Scalar-first quaternion (length 4).

tol

Tolerance for matrix validation.

Value

A robot_rotation object.

Details

  • x: a rotation matrix, robot_rotation, or robot_quaternion;

  • axis and angle: active right-handed rotation by angle radians about the unit vector axis (any nonzero vector is normalized);

  • angle alone: a planar rotation (SO(2));

  • euler with sequence: intrinsic Euler angles, so sequence = "ZYX" and euler = c(a, b, c) gives \(R_z(a) R_y(b) R_x(c)\) (yaw, pitch, roll). The URDF rpy = c(r, p, y) attribute corresponds to sequence = "ZYX" with euler = c(y, p, r);

  • rotvec: a rotation vector \(\theta u\);

  • quaternion: scalar-first c(w, x, y, z).

Matrices are checked for \(R^\top R = I\) and \(\det R = 1\) within tol; use orthonormalize() first to repair accumulated drift.

Examples

R <- robot_rotation(axis = c(0, 0, 1), angle = pi / 2)
R
#> <robot_rotation> SO(3)
#> angle 1.5708 rad about axis (0, 0, 1)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    0   -1    0
#> [2,]    1    0    0
#> [3,]    0    0    1
robot_rotation(euler = c(0.3, -0.2, 0.1), sequence = "ZYX")
#> <robot_rotation> SO(3)
#> angle 0.381565 rad about axis (0.3379, -0.4807, 0.8092)
#>        [,1]    [,2]    [,3]
#> [1,] 0.9363 -0.3130 -0.1593
#> [2,] 0.2896  0.9447 -0.1538
#> [3,] 0.1987  0.0978  0.9752
robot_rotation(angle = pi / 6)
#> <robot_rotation> SO(2)
#> angle 0.523599 rad
#>       [,1]   [,2]
#> [1,] 0.866 -0.500
#> [2,] 0.500  0.866
